blocks.html: B2B (Business-to-Business) refers to commercial transactions in which one business sells products or services to another business, rather than to individual consumers. These transactions often involve higher-value deals, longer sales cycles, and multiple stakeholders compared to B2C (Business-to-Consumer) interactions.

B2B is a fundamental model across industries such as manufacturing, technology, healthcare, and professional services. Unlike B2C, where decisions are often driven by personal preferences, B2B purchasing decisions are typically based on logic, ROI, efficiency, and long-term value. This makes relationship-building, trust, and expertise critical in B2B engagements.
B2B transactions follow a structured and strategic process:

items.title: Need Identification
items.html: A business identifies a challenge or requirement.

items.title: Vendor Research
items.html: Multiple vendors are evaluated based on capabilities and credibility.

items.title: Stakeholder Involvement
items.html: Decision-making involves various roles such as executives, procurement teams, and technical experts.

items.title: Proposal & Negotiation
items.html: Vendors submit proposals, followed by pricing and contract negotiations.

items.title: Purchase & Implementation
items.html: Once finalized, the solution is deployed and integrated into business operations.

blocks.html: Decisions take time due to complexity and approvals.
Deals are typically larger and more strategic.
Trust and long-term partnerships are essential.
Offerings are often tailored to business needs.

items.html: Predictable Revenue Streams: Long-term contracts ensure stability.
Higher Customer Lifetime Value (CLV): Repeat business and renewals are common.
Scalable Growth: Opportunities to expand within existing accounts.
Strategic Partnerships: Collaboration drives innovation and efficiency.

blocks.html: A software company provides customer relationship management (CRM) solutions to enterprises. Instead of selling to individuals, it works with corporate clients, engaging stakeholders such as sales leaders, IT teams, and finance departments to close high-value contracts and deliver customized solutions.

B2B focuses on delivering value-driven solutions to businesses through strategic, relationship-oriented selling. It requires a deep understanding of client needs, structured processes, and collaboration across multiple stakeholders.
